_doc: Source for scripts/build_paste_bundles.py. Each bundle is one round: a self-contained PowerShell text the PFM copies from its raw page and pastes into Windows PowerShell ISE (F5). It writes the files, then opens the 90-161.Z Deployer (a window; text prompts if no window can open): steps run one by one with a live log and PASS/FAIL counts, then one results folder (Rounds\\<round>: a report file plus copies of the PDFs, to attach to one e-mail; zips do not cross the boundary) and a summary for the clipboard. It runs only the steps inside it (PFM 3A). A step's "default" may be {passed, paths}: the step is ticked only when those files changed since the round that passed it; after a round passes it, set passed to the new hash (PFM 14 Nov 26). Never hand-edit scripts/gov/paste/*.ps1: change this file or the sources and rebuild. A step may list "needs" (check ids in the engine's $checkDefs) and "estimate" (minutes, used until a real run time exists). "apps" is the embedded catalog the Choose screen lists (name, plain-English summary, step names); without it, one application has every step.

bundles.title: Round R16: solution import test r2 (T17, values from the T05 export), probe r5 (Contribute to the coworker's own user), site setup r5 (header logo and thumbnail set apart, each checked)

steps.name: T17 Solution import test r2
steps.note: You import one small test solution in Power Automate and run its flow (about 5 minutes, an estimate). r2 uses the values of your T05 export; r1 failed with an XML error in R15.
steps.url_source: Microsoft Learn, Power Automate US Government (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/us-govt): DoD maker portal; editable in the window, remembered in Config (agent value, PFM to confirm in R13)
guide: 1. Select Open in browser. Power Automate opens; sign in with your CAC if asked.
2. In the left menu select Solutions (under More if you do not see it), then Import solution > Browse.
3. In the File name box press Ctrl+V (the file path is on the clipboard), select Open, then Next.
4. Connections: for SharePoint pick your existing connection. Environment variable "Site URL": paste the new site address. Select Import.
5. Wait for "Successfully imported" (1-3 minutes, an estimate). Open the solution "90-161.Z solution import test",
open the flow "90161Z T17 Solution Import Test r2", select Run, then Run flow.
6. Come back here and select "Done: the run has started".
If the import fails: copy its error message (no names or site address) into the results e-mail, then select Skip this step.

steps.name: T11 Rights probe r5: import and run the flow
steps.note: You import and run the probe r5 flow (about 5 minutes, an estimate). It sends no e-mail; it gives the coworker's own user Contribute on a test list, reads the coworker's rights there, then deletes the test list.
steps.url_source: Microsoft Learn, Power Automate US Government (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/us-govt): DoD maker portal; editable in the window, remembered in Config (agent value, PFM to confirm in R13)
guide: 1. In Power Automate select My flows > Import > Import Package (Legacy).
2. Select Upload. In the File name box press Ctrl+V (the file path is on the clipboard), then select Open.
3. For the SharePoint connection select your existing one. Select Import.
4. Open "90161Z T11 Rights Probe r5" and select Run. Enter:
Site address: the new site.  Coworker e-mail: the same coworker as last time (a typical wing user).
5. Come back here and select "Done: the run has started". Site setup collects the result when the flow finishes.
If Power Automate is already open, skip Open in browser.

steps.name: T16 Site setup
steps.note: Asks for the site address and a CAC sign-in, sets the header logo and the thumbnail (each by its own call), checks the site settings, and collects both flow results (waits up to 15 minutes for each).

apps.name: 90-161.Z: Publications and Forms Management
apps.summary: Test round R16. Tests the solution import again (r2), tests app-user rights, and sets the site logo and thumbnail.
steps: T11 Rights probe r5: import and run the flow
